To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the secular variation in Sicilian geomagnetic field direction during the past 800 years is in good agreement with the European curve, that the historical ages of Etna lavas are in error by a few centuries and that this has implications for eruptive models based solely on historical records.

the geomagnetic secular variation in southern Italy during historic times is well documented and agrees with the variation observed elsewhere in Europe; the palaeomagnetic and archaeomagnetic data provide an independent means of determining the age of volcanic products, and of archaeological structures, in southern Italy; and the ages of lavas from Mount Etne are much older than previously believed, which casts doubts on the eruptive models that are based on historical records.
the geomagnetic secular variation in the area surrounding Mount Etna has been determined and that the ages of many of the historically dated lavas are much older than previously thought.

the historical record of Etna is not as reliable as previously thought and that it is not possible to use the historical record alone as a basis for eruptive models.
